One-line distribution of each column

Source: R/utils_print.R
pr_spark.Rd

Print one line per column: its name, a sparkline of its distribution, a short summary and the share of missing values, for a quick look at a data set before modelling.

Usage

pr_spark(data, vars = NULL, bins = 12, indent = 2)

Arguments

data

A data frame (tibbles included).

vars

Character. Columns to show; NULL (default) shows all.

bins

Positive integer. Histogram bins, and the most levels drawn for a categorical column (default 12).

indent

Non-negative integer. Spaces before each line (default 2). Must leave at least twelve console columns for the name and missing share.

Value

The printed lines, invisibly.

Details

Numeric columns show a histogram of bins equal-width bins over the finite values, with their mean and SD (3 significant digits); whole numbers with no more distinct values than bins get one bar per value, so no empty bin falls between two values. Date and date-time columns show the same histogram with their first and last dates. Factor, character and logical columns show their level counts (in level order, or the bins most frequent levels when there are more), the number of levels and the most frequent one with its share of non-missing values; one whose values all differ, such as an identifier, shows how many there are. Other columns show their class only. SPSS user-missing values are excluded from summaries and counted in the missing share, consistently with ordinary missing values. Shorter scientific notation is used for extreme numeric summaries. Centering and scaling retain finite spread at extreme magnitudes, and narrow integer64 ranges retain their differences before double conversion. Empty columns show empty with an unavailable missing share; entirely missing columns and columns without finite values are identified separately, without a most-frequent level or undefined percentage. Lines that do not fit the console use a compact summary that retains the missing share; long names and summary text are shortened with an ellipsis. The default includes each column by position, even when names repeat. Missing and empty column names display as <NA> and "".

See also

Other print helpers: pr_badge(), pr_box(), pr_head(), pr_kv(), pr_note(), pr_section(), pr_table(), pr_tree()

Examples

set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(age = rnorm(200, 56, 11),
                 stage = factor(sample(c("I", "II", "III"), 200, TRUE)),
                 size_mm = rlnorm(200, 2.6, 0.5))
pr_spark(df)
#>   age      ▁▂▃▄██▆▆▄▃▁▂  mean 56.4  sd 10.2        NA 0.0%
#>   stage    █▇▇           3 levels · top I (37.5%)  NA 0.0%
#>   size_mm  ▇█▅▃▂▁▁▁▁▁▁▁  mean 15.5  sd 9.00        NA 0.0%
